q: Which field of `Config` encodes the whole layering design?
options: `config_paths: Vec<PathBuf>` — later entries take precedence, writes go to the last
`guard: Mutex<()>` — one lock per config tier
`secrets: SecretStorage` — secrets decide merge order
`secrets_cache` — cached values override files
explanation: The mutex serializes mutation, it encodes no tiering.
Secrets are stored separately, they don't drive precedence.
The cache holds decrypted secrets, not merged view override rules.

q: Where does system-level config live on Windows, per `system_config_path()` in base.rs?
options: `%PROGRAMDATA%\goose\config.yaml`
`C:\Windows\goose.yaml`
`%APPDATA%\goose\config.toml`
`C:\goose\config.json`
explanation: The resolver never writes under C:\Windows.
The format is YAML in v1.49.0, and APPDATA is not used for the system tier.
Wrong path and wrong format — no JSON system config exists.

q: `Config::global()` returns `&'static Config`. What does that promise?
options: One process-wide singleton, initialized once from the default path set
A new Config instance on every call
Config values can change freely mid-process without synchronization
The config is immutable forever
explanation: It memoizes via OnceCell — repeated calls return the same instance.
Mutation is allowed but goes through the Mutex guard; the reference stays stable.
Set-param calls exist (e.g. set_goose_thinking_effort), so not immutable.

q: What does the code print? `Config::global().get_param::<u32>("GOOSE_MAX_TURNS").unwrap_or(DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS)` when the config value is the string `"four"`:
options: It returns DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS only if the read became an Err; a type mismatch produces an Err, so the fallback wins
It panics on every call
It returns 1000 always, ignoring config
It coerces "four" into 4
explanation: get_param converts to Result; unwrap_or absorbs the Err instead of panicking.
The fallback is DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS (1000) as defined in agent.rs:90 — but only when the read errors or the key is absent.
Typed reads never silently parse strings into numbers.

q: Why does `legacy_thinking_effort()` still exist at base.rs:1370?
options: It maps the old CLAUDE_THINKING_TYPE values into modern ThinkingEffort so pre-migration configs keep working
It is a leftover debug helper nobody uses
It writes new config files in the old format
It detects Claude-specific models for the UI
explanation: It is called by get_goose_thinking_effort as a fallback — actively used.
It reads legacy keys, it does not write any file.
Model detection is provider-layer logic, not config migration.

q: Both agent paths read GOOSE_MAX_TURNS. The parity risk is:
options: Each path has its own fallback chain; changing enforcement in one path leaves behavior divergent under GOOSE_STATE_MACHINE=1
The reads deadlock because both call Config::global()
The key can only be read once per process
The state machine path cannot see u32 values
explanation: Config::global() is a cheap OnceCell read, no deadlock involved.
Keys are read repeatedly all over the codebase.
The state machine value goes into MaxTurnsOperation::new(max_turns) as a u32.

q: Which change unblocks this runtime error? — `ConfigError: invalid type: string "4"` while a legacy test sets GOOSE_MAX_TURNS via env var, but a new code path reads it with `get_param::<u32>`:
options: A migration that normalizes the env value to a number (or the consumer switching to a type-agnostic read with explicit parsing)
Delete the legacy test
Change every read site to `.unwrap_or(4)`
Set `resolver = "2"` in Cargo.toml
explanation: Deleting coverage is never the fix for a runtime contract change.
Hardcoding 4 makes the key meaningless — the fallback must stay DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS.
The resolver controls feature unification, not config parsing.
